registry snapshot digest is immutable and duplicate tool ids fail closed
selection plan carries required capability and M5.4 admission requirement but does not perform admission

numeric requests prefer issuer authority over lower-authority leads
commercial gap requests stop instead of searching for an unlicensed proxy

resolved_findings.finding: A route string alone could select a cheap but low-authority source for an exact numeric request.
resolved_findings.repair: Planner filters by role-specific minimum authority before cost-aware deterministic ordering.

resolved_findings.finding: A planner could treat an in-memory allowlist as a real execution authorization.
resolved_findings.repair: The plan marks every selected step execution_admission=required_m5_4_capability_check; no admission or invocation API exists in M6.2.

resolved_findings.finding: Commercial gaps and exhausted routes might silently fall back to a public proxy or unbounded search.
resolved_findings.repair: Zero call budget/commercial gap is terminal; missing eligible routes return typed route_exhausted rather than a free search.

resolved_findings.finding: A planner could fabricate ToolInvocationReceipt without a tool call.
resolved_findings.repair: M6.2 creates ToolSelectionPlan steps only; invocation receipts remain absent until a separately admitted executor exists.

open_followups: M6.3 owns CandidateBundle retrieval/reranking and must separately prove metadata/neighbor/table behavior.
Any future M6.2 executor must call M5.4/M5.5 in its actual mutation/invocation transaction; a selection plan alone is not authorization.
No provider, network, external tool, Evidence Gate, parser, Writer/full-chain, business Case mutation or legacy authority change is admitted.
